subject: System Design
title: What Is a Distributed System
description: A 60-second lesson on What Is a Distributed System.

hook.text: A distributed system is a group of computers that appear to the user as a single coherent system.

buildup.text: Google Search runs on thousands of machines, yet you see one search box and one result page.

discovery.text: Distribution provides fault tolerance, scalability, and geographic proximity that one machine can't offer.

twist.text: Distribution also brings partial failures: one node can fail while others keep running. Debugging becomes nightmarish.

climax.text: A distributed system trades simplicity for capability. Every benefit comes with a new class of problems.

punchline.text: Many machines, one illusion — and many hidden problems.

quiz.question: What defines a distributed system?
options: Multiple computers appearing as one coherent system to users
